records.availability: Public HackerOne bounty program active; no pause banner observed.
in_scope_assets: Recon Data (official ListDomains and ListIPs endpoints)
scope_conditions: The ubereats wildcard excludes every separately listed out-of-scope host.
Recon data is informational and does not make every returned asset bounty-eligible.
Reports must contain analysis, validation, reasoning and demonstrable security impact rather than scanner output.
Researchers may test only accounts they own and must minimize any access to other users' data.
The uber.com row is recorded as Domain, not rewritten as a wildcard. Exact subdomain coverage must be established before a vulnerability test.
The scope table excludes Fraud Reports, including free rides and payment evasion. Its narrower exclusion controls this work despite broader fraud examples in the policy prose.
The Merchants exception distinguishes same-organization role changes (excluded) from cross-tenant issues; this plan does not test merchants.
records.automation: Unvalidated scan/enumeration output is excluded. This is not an explicit blanket ban on every automated tool. Permission and suitability for ScopeGuard recurring production comparisons have not been established; no Uber target or automatic profile is enabled by this review.
records.request_limit_note: No numerical testing request limit found in the official policy or scope table read. Null means unknown, not unlimited.
records.accounts: Only owned personal/test accounts may be used. Reports are expected by default to identify the researcher with a @wearehackerone.com alias. Uber supplies no preconfigured test account when no test-account instructions are published. The inspected login page offers phone/email and Google; no account was signed in or created.
excluded_assets: merchants.ubereats.com (same-organization role escalation; cross-tenant issues remain eligible)
exclusions: Brute force, denial of service, social engineering and destructive testing
Automated output without manual validation and impact
Missing headers, TLS configuration, open ports, banners and versions without a security exploit
Rate-limit observations without demonstrated security impact
Accessing or changing other users' data beyond the minimum proof
Free-ride, payment-evasion and other fraud reports are explicitly excluded in the scope table.
Reports based only on a public login panel or missing non-authentication cookie flags have no established security impact.

research_plan.summary: Public preparation is complete. An Uber account sign-in is needed before examining a private test resource.
research_plan.goal: Evaluate whether a non-financial private test record is protected from anonymous access and, if suitable, a second separately owned account. This is a hypothesis, not a discovered vulnerability.
completed: Re-read the official policy and all 24 scope rows: four in scope and 20 excluded/conditional rows.
Identified exclusions relevant to this work: raw scanner reports, missing-header-only observations, account enumeration, brute force, disruption and fraud.
Inspected the ordinary public homepage and the official sign-in form without entering credentials or requesting a verification code.
Validated the existing access-comparison method against local synthetic and loopback fixtures; no Uber endpoint was used in these tests.
user_actions: When available, complete secure sign-in for an Uber account you own. Only you can complete its phone/email verification; do not send passwords or verification codes in chat.
Confirm your existing HackerOne username so the expected researcher alias can be documented. No new HackerOne account is needed.
Only if we proceed to the two-account comparison, make a second separately owned test account available through secure sign-in. One account is enough to begin mapping the first test.
blockers: Owned Uber account access and the researcher HackerOne identity are not available in the current browser.
No exact private test resource, endpoint, synthetic marker or intended-access baseline has been observed; a URL will not be guessed or activated.
A two-account comparison additionally needs a second separately owned account without shared access to the chosen synthetic record.
The official ListDomains URL with offset=0 and limit=20 was inaccessible through the web research tool. No returned asset list was obtained or used.
No numerical request limit was found; the proposed small request budget is an internal ceiling, not permission from Uber.
planned_checks: After sign-in, map a non-financial private feature through its normal interface and verify the exact resource URL against current scope. Stop if it needs a ride, purchase, payment change, other-person data or an excluded asset.
Use only a synthetic non-sensitive test value, confirm intended privacy and obtain a successful owner control. Do not use trip history, real addresses or payment information as test material.
If the exact read-only method is permitted, compare the same owned resource without login. A login page, redirect or failed owner control is inconclusive, not a bug.
If a second owned account is available, check only the known first-account resource against that account and repeat both owner controls. Never guess identifiers or enumerate accounts.

Keep any eventual single validation bounded to at most six read-only requests. That ceiling is a local planning choice, not a published Uber limit or permission for recurring checks. Stop on rate limits, server errors, unexpected data or unclear scope.
Retain only minimal redacted evidence. Confirm account separation, expected permissions, reproducibility and actual impact before drafting any report; no submission is enabled by these notes.
research_plan.validation: 25 local tests passed: test_accessmatrix, test_accesscheck and test_policyevidence. Fixtures cover blocked access, deliberately exposed synthetic data, failed controls, non-JSON/redirect responses, revocation, request limits and redaction. They do not measure Uber security.
research_plan.result: Live Uber vulnerability tests: 0. Confirmed Uber bugs: 0. Public policy and entry-page research only. No account creation, messages, rides, purchases, report submission or additional spending.
